points.description: States TRUE (the statement is correct: a user process cannot force a context switch to a chosen READY process).

Justification: the user process has no control over which process the scheduler picks next; scheduling/context-switch decisions are made by the OS scheduler (kernel), not by user processes, even if the PID is known.
points.partial_credit: 1 mark if justification is vague or only partly correct (e.g. says only that the OS decides, or that user mode lacks privilege, without linking to the scheduler choosing the next process).

rubric.notes: Full marks need TRUE plus a correct justification that the scheduler (OS/kernel), not the user process, chooses the next process, so knowing the PID gives no control. If the justification is missing or wrong, give 0 overall, as the question states. Give part marks for TRUE with a vague or incomplete justification; FALSE earns nothing.
